tasks.short: Establish and communicate lesson, unit and project objectives

steps.what: Select curriculum aims and determine the intended learning for the class
Write clear objectives for lessons, units and projects

loop.purpose: Express selected learning intent as clear objectives
loop.input: Teacher-selected aims, intended learning, age level and lesson or project scope
loop.output: Draft objectives with explicit aim references
loop.check: Teacher checks curriculum meaning, appropriate challenge, observable learning and missing or invented requirements; code matching alone is insufficient
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsuitable objectives are rewritten by the teacher
loop.why_not_simpler: Native objective banks are reused first; adapting language to a specific learning intent still needs language judgement

steps.what: Verify final objectives and communicate them clearly to students

tasks.design: Reuse objective banks in {DOCS} first, then draft wording only for teacher-selected learning intent. The teacher checks the final meaning and communicates it to students; the tool does not choose learning level or assess pupils.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clear wording takes composition time after the teacher has chosen what pupils should learn.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language tool can suggest alternative wording from a defined brief.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right challenge and checking that students understand the intended learning.
tasks.human_edge: Link an objective to this class's prior understanding and explain why it matters.
tasks.altitude: Less objective composition; curriculum and classroom decisions remain with the teacher.

reach.task: Review objective wording across a unit
reach.learn: Curriculum progression and observable learning evidence

evidence.claim: A trial with 259 English secondary science teachers found lower weekly planning time with a guided language tool; this is context, not a measured objective-writing saving.
Drafting wording from teacher-selected learning intent is plausible and requires semantic review.

assumptions: Boundary is establishing and communicating objectives, not whole lesson planning, teaching or assessment. Overlapping preparation work is allocated once.

The teacher produces aim identifier and exact text, intended learning, learner age, scope and prerequisites in s1, including capture and checking. No clean curriculum-to-class mapping is assumed upstream; missing information returns to manual objective writing.
Test native objective banks and document structures before model use. No identifiable pupil records are needed for the brief.
Final verification before classroom use is counted in s3; changing intent or wording requires renewed review.
The shares and reduction are E1 scenarios to validate locally.
unknowns: Existing objective banks and actual composition time
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce objective composition while preserving curriculum meaning and appropriate challenge?

already_counted.description: Learning selection, final verification and communication remain.

incremental.description: Teacher reviews objective-bank changes and samples draft fidelity.

approvals.approved_version: Exact objective wording, selected curriculum aims and class-level brief reviewed before communication; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 less three upkeep hours gives net=17. High assumes wording effort halves; low assumes manual rewriting leaves only upkeep-equivalent gain. Learning selection and communication retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select and assign lessons and prepare explicit keys for closed homework questions
Correct closed homework questions against the teacher's explicit answer key
Correct open homework answers and resolve ambiguous closed responses
Check final homework corrections and return feedback to students

tasks.design: Configure native closed-question checking in {LMS} using the teacher's explicit key and digital submissions. Open responses and unmatched answers remain manually corrected, and the teacher checks the final feedback before returning it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exact-key checking can consume correction time even though it needs no judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native learning-system quizzes can match explicit answers and flag unmatched responses.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting reasoning, recognising a valid alternative and giving useful feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the misconception behind an answer instead of relying on a correctness flag.
tasks.altitude: Less closed-item checking; assignment choices, open marking and feedback release stay with the teacher.

reach.task: Use teacher-verified misconceptions to plan extra practice
reach.learn: Item intent and avoiding conclusions from a single response

evidence.claim: Explicit-key checking of closed questions can run deterministically without a model judging open answers.

assumptions: Boundary covers assigning and correcting formative homework, not consequential assessment or placement. Closed questions account for 25 percent of baseline time only in this E1 scenario.

The teacher produces question identifiers, accepted answers, units, exact matching rules and key version in s1, including capture and verification. Students produce question-linked digital responses as existing homework work, with no extra student capture assumed. Paper submissions remain manually corrected; no free transcription or uncertain handwriting extraction is presumed.

Roster ownership and identifiers come from existing school administration outside this boundary, unchanged; the teacher checks assignment and submission identity. Missing identity, units or unrecognised responses go to s3, never guessed marks.

Test native quiz functions first. Teacher final review in s4 checks key applicability, flagged cases and all returned results; no automated pupil ranking or model-based learning-outcome decision is introduced.
Any extension to consequential marks requires a separately assessed design, access and national school consultation process.
unknowns: Closed-item share, native checking already in use and digital submission coverage
research_questions: Does native exact-key checking agree with teacher correction on units, alternatives and malformed answers after exceptions are counted?

already_counted.description: Assignment and key capture, open correction and final feedback review remain.

incremental.description: Teacher audits key changes, matching rules and correction defects.
Learning-system administrator maintains quiz permissions and tests updates.

approvals.approved_version: Exact learner-bound feedback, submission snapshot, key version and teacher corrections; edits require renewed release review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 less three focal upkeep hours gives net=22. High assumes the stated closed-item checking transfers fully; low assumes paper work, existing automation and exceptions leave only upkeep-equivalent gains. Open correction and final review retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tutor students and prepare and deliver remedial support

steps.what: Identify the student's difficulty and select a remedial learning objective
Prepare and check remedial examples and practice materials

loop.purpose: Adapt practice wording to a teacher-identified difficulty
loop.input: Generic learning objective, source examples and chosen scaffolding
loop.output: Draft worked example and short practice set with answers
loop.check: Teacher solves the items and checks factual accuracy, level, scaffolding and whether the draft addresses the identified difficulty without changing the concept
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsuitable items are rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse existing practice first; explaining the same concept with different wording or examples needs language judgement

steps.what: Tutor students, implement remedial support and check their developing understanding

tasks.design: Reuse suitable practice in {DOCS} before using a bounded loop to adapt missing examples. The teacher identifies the difficulty, verifies the final items before use and retains tutoring and learning checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Making a suitable example takes preparation time after the learning difficulty is understood.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors can rewrite material at another level; this supports preparation rather than diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding why the student is struggling and responding to their next explanation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a simpler explanation misses the real difficulty and change approach.

ambition.what: Offer a short teacher-checked practice set between remedial meetings

tasks.altitude: Less material adaptation; no change in tutoring time or pupil-support decisions.

reach.task: Deliver a teacher-defined remedial practice activity
reach.learn: Scaffolding, misconception checks and when to refer back

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another level, as described in the digest.
Using adapted material for remedial practice requires teacher checking and does not establish a saving in live tutoring.

assumptions: Boundary covers identifying a difficulty, preparing practice and tutoring, not diagnosing a disability or setting a formal support placement.

The teacher produces the remedial objective, intended scaffolding and selected source examples in s1, with capture and interpretation counted. The model receives generic material and no identifiable student record; missing information returns to teacher preparation.
Native practice banks and rewriting tools are tested first. Source concepts, answers and final item versions are checked in s2 and released before use at the start of s3.
Preparation overlaps other lesson-planning tasks; the same materials cannot yield additive savings in a roll-up.
The new optional practice service uses released capacity and is not counted as additional saving.
unknowns: Available practice banks and actual adaptation burden
research_questions: Does checked adaptation reduce preparation while keeping every worked example and answer correct?

already_counted.description: Difficulty assessment and live remedial support remain.

incremental.description: Teacher audits adapted items and refreshes source materials.

approvals.approved_version: Exact practice items, worked solutions, source version and intended remedial objective checked before use; edits require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less three upkeep hours gives net=7. High assumes adaptation time halves; low assumes extra correction leaves only upkeep-equivalent gains. Assessment and tutoring keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with families and colleagues to resolve academic or behaviour problems

steps.what: Review specific academic or behavioural concerns and prepare facts for discussion
Confer with parents, guardians, teachers, counselors or administrators and agree support actions

tasks.design: Retain factual preparation and direct problem-solving with families and colleagues. Existing {LMS} and {DOCS} records support the discussion; no behavioural label or resolution is generated automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different participants may have incomplete or conflicting views of the problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can support factual review without resolving disagreement.
tasks.still_hard: Building trust, understanding context and choosing feasible support.
tasks.human_edge: Hear the pupil's and family's perspectives and avoid turning limited observations into labels.
tasks.altitude: Support discussion and escalation rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify a support question before specialist consultation
reach.learn: Factual observations, consent and limits of classroom interpretation

evidence.claim: Resolving academic or behavioural concerns requires contextual dialogue and human judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers teacher preparation and substantive discussion, not other participants' time, a formal diagnosis or separately measured meeting administration.

The teacher produces observations through existing teaching and checks their meaning in s1. Participants supply accounts during s2. No structured behavioural code or free case summary is assumed; gaps are clarified directly within retained work.
Native record access is reviewed before any future custom tool; no new capture, recording or pupil evaluation system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the process is unchanged. Shared support encounters must be allocated once across related tasks.
unknowns: Support process, information-sharing rules and participant responsibilities
research_questions: Which unresolved concerns stem from disagreement rather than unavailable records?

already_counted.description: Factual preparation and support conversation remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine support discussion and disputed concerns retain preparation and conversation; no assumed paperwork saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Drafting objectives and remedial materials and checking explicitly keyed homework can reduce limited preparation work; teaching, support decisions and family discussions remain human.
reach: Review curriculum progression with instructional coordinators
Guide tutors using teacher-verified learning needs
Clarify support questions with special education teachers
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who offers checked practice sooner and spends the necessary time understanding students, without delegating learning-level or support decisions.

job.title: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
